title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (II)

articles.content_en: Article 1 In property insurance, where different applicants respectively insure the same subject matter of insurance, and after an insured event occurs, the insured claims insurance compensation pursuant to the insurance contract within the scope of his or her insurable interest, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 2 In personal insurance, where an insurance contract is void because the applicant has no insurable interest in the insured, and the applicant requests the insurer to refund the insurance premium after deducting the corresponding handling fees, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 3 Where, when concluding an insurance contract, the applicant or the applicant's agent fails to sign or affix a seal personally, and the insurer or the insurer's agent signs or affixes a seal on behalf of the applicant, the contract shall not take effect with respect to the applicant. However, if the applicant has already paid the insurance premium, it shall be deemed that the applicant has ratified the act of signing or affixing a seal on his or her behalf.
Where the insurer or the insurer's agent fills in the insurance policy documents on behalf of the applicant and the applicant subsequently confirms by signing or affixing a seal, the content so filled in shall be deemed the true expression of intention of the applicant. However, this shall not apply where there is evidence proving that the insurer or the insurer's agent falls under any of the circumstances provided for in Article 116 or Article 131 of the Insurance Law.

Article 4 Where an insurer accepts the application form submitted by the applicant and collects the insurance premium, but has not yet expressed its intention as to whether to underwrite the insurance, and an insured event occurs, and the insured or beneficiary requests the insurer to bear liability for compensation or payment of insurance money in accordance with the insurance contract, if the conditions for underwriting are met, the People's Court shall support the claim; if the conditions for underwriting are not met, the insurer shall not bear insurance liability, but shall refund the insurance premium already collected.
Where the insurer claims that the conditions for underwriting are not met, the insurer shall bear the burden of adducing evidence.

Article 5 At the time of conclusion of an insurance contract, the circumstances relating to the subject matter of insurance or the insured known to the applicant fall within the content that the applicant "shall truthfully disclose" as provided for in Article 16, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law.

Article 6 The applicant's obligation of disclosure shall be limited to the scope and content inquired by the insurer. Where the parties dispute the scope and content of inquiry, the insurer bears the burden of adducing evidence.
Where the insurer requests dissolution of the contract on the ground that the applicant violated the obligation of truthful disclosure with respect to the general clauses listed in the questionnaire of the application form, the People's Court shall not support the claim, except where such general clause has specific content.

Article 7 Where, after the formation of the insurance contract, the insurer knew or should have known that the applicant had failed to perform the obligation of truthful disclosure, and nevertheless collected the insurance premium, and then claims dissolution of the contract in accordance with Article 16, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 8 Where the insurer, without exercising the right to dissolve the contract, directly refuses to pay compensation on the ground that the circumstances provided for in Article 16, Paragraph 4 or Paragraph 5 of the Insurance Law exist, the People's Court shall not support the claim, except where the parties have otherwise reached an agreement on the matter of refusal to pay compensation and the continuation of the insurance contract.

Article 9 Clauses such as liability exemption clauses, deductibles, deductible rates, proportional compensation or payment, and other clauses in the standard form contract text provided by the insurer that exempt or mitigate the insurer's liability may be recognized as "clauses exempting the insurer from liability" as provided for in Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law.
Clauses under which the insurer enjoys the right to dissolve the contract because the applicant or the insured violates statutory or agreed obligations shall not fall within the "clauses exempting the insurer from liability" as provided for in Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law.

Article 10 Where an insurer takes the circumstances of prohibitive provisions in laws and administrative regulations as the grounds for exemption under an exemption clause of an insurance contract, after the insurer has drawn attention to the clause, if the applicant, insured, or beneficiary claims on the ground that the insurer failed to perform the obligation of clear explanation that the clause does not become part of the contract, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 11 Where, at the time of conclusion of the insurance contract, the insurer, on the application form, insurance policy, or other insurance certificates, draws attention to the clauses exempting the insurer from liability in the insurance contract by means of words, fonts, symbols, or other obvious marks sufficient to attract the applicant's attention, the People's Court shall determine that the insurer has performed the obligation of drawing attention as provided for in Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law.
Where the insurer explains to the applicant in written or oral form the concepts, content, and legal consequences of the clauses exempting the insurer from liability in the insurance contract in a manner understandable to an ordinary person, the People's Court shall determine that the insurer has performed the obligation of clear explanation as provided for in Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Insurance Law.

Article 12 For an insurance contract concluded through the Internet, telephone, or other means, if the insurer draws attention to and clearly explains the clauses exempting the insurer from liability in the form of web pages, audio, video, or other forms, the People's Court may determine that the insurer has performed the obligations of drawing attention and clear explanation.

Article 13 The insurer shall bear the burden of adducing evidence that it has performed the obligation of clear explanation.
Where the applicant confirms by signing, affixing a seal, or in other forms on relevant documents that the insurer has performed the obligation of clear explanation meeting the requirements of Article 11, Paragraph 2 of this Interpretation, it shall be determined that the insurer has performed that obligation, except where other evidence proves that the insurer has not performed the obligation of clear explanation.

Article 15 The thirty-day period for verification provided for in Article 23 of the Insurance Law shall be counted from the date on which the insurer first receives the claim request and the relevant certificates and materials provided by the applicant, the insured, or the beneficiary.
Where the insurer claims to deduct the period during which the applicant, the insured, or the beneficiary supplements the relevant certificates and materials, the People's Court shall support the claim. The deducted period shall run from the date on which the notice made by the insurer in accordance with Article 22 of the Insurance Law reaches the applicant, the insured, or the beneficiary, to the date on which the relevant certificates and materials supplemented by the applicant, the insured, or the beneficiary in accordance with the notice requirements reach the insurer.

Article 16 The insurer shall exercise the right of subrogation in its own name.
In accordance with Article 60, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law, the limitation of action for the insurer's right of subrogation shall be counted from the date on which it obtains the right of subrogation.

Article 17 Where the insurer's interpretation of non-insurance terms in the standard clauses of the insurance contract provided by it conforms to professional meaning, or, although not conforming to professional meaning, is favorable to the applicant, the insured, or the beneficiary, the People's Court shall recognize it.

Article 18 For documents such as road traffic accident determination letters and fire accident determination letters produced by administrative departments in accordance with legal provisions, the People's Court shall examine them according to law and confirm their corresponding evidentiary weight, except where contrary evidence can overturn them.

Article 19 After an insured event occurs, where the insured or the beneficiary brings a prosecution against the insurer, and the insurer defends on the ground that the insured or the beneficiary has not demanded the third party to bear liability, the People's Court shall not support the defense.
After a property insurance event occurs, where the insured brings an action for the shortfall after obtaining compensation from the third party for the losses suffered and requests the insurer to compensate, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Article 20 A branch established by an insurance company according to law and having obtained a business license falls within the category of "other organizations" as provided for in Article 48 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and may participate in litigation as a party in a case of insurance contract dispute.

Article 21 For cases of insurance contract disputes that have not yet been finally adjudicated after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall apply; for cases that have already been finally adjudicated before this Interpretation comes into force and for which a party applies for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the adjudication supervision procedure, this Interpretation shall not apply.
